title: Timeout-controlled runner machine
statement: Let $H$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over alphabet $\Gamma$ with state set $Q$, and let $S$ be a finite type. Given a function assigning a state in $Q$ to each optional element of $S$, the definition forms a phase-host machine that starts in the true phase at $H$’s initial state and uses $H$ in that phase. Whenever the current state equals the assigned state for some element of $S$, the phase transition switches to the false phase; in the false phase the machine has a singleton state and makes stationary, nonwriting self-loops.
